item.title: Hackers say stolen Rosstat data shows 450,100 Russian military deaths
item.description: The claim rests on leaked death certificates that Rosstat says were not compromised. At least 168 public datasets have vanished from the agency's collections.

item.title: Ten northern European countries to run their navies as one force
item.description: The 10 November pact would let parts, ammunition and crews swap across the ten navies. Norway's PM calls it a response to US cuts to aircraft and submarines offered to NATO.

item.title: EU and Canada launch Alliance for the Future, covering security
item.description: Canada becomes the first non-European country in the EU's Safe defence procurement scheme, with contracts already won by Canadian firms in Poland and Latvia.

item.title: French minister accuses Mélenchon of speaking for the Kremlin over Donbas vote
item.description: Jean-Noël Barrot says the vote plan would merely repeat Putin's justification for the war, and rejects claims that aid to Ukraine is to blame for French purchasing-power problems.

item.title: Colau plans 2% tax on wealth over a million euros
item.description: Her Frente Amplio says the Barcelona plan would push more than 500,000 homes back onto the market. Rents hit by it would fall 31% on average.

item.title: Prices won the election. Europe still has no shield for port pay.
item.description: The tariffs that squeeze our freight and shifts survived the midterms untouched, because no Congress gets a vote on them. The Commission and member states owe port workers a costed plan before year end.

item.title: SAJ commander Igor Žmirić held for up to 30 days over torture claims
item.description: The Belgrade court ordered detention of the police unit chief, who faces suspicion of abuse and torture. Lawyers say the arrests before the elections look political; the chief prosecutor denies it.

item.title: AI makes cyberattacks faster and bigger, Dutch safety service warns
item.description: The NCTV says state hackers from Russia, China, Iran and North Korea target the Netherlands. The cabinet has presented a programme to strengthen digital resilience, including a screening service called the AI-wasstraat.

item.title: A war Massie says nobody voted for, costing us all
item.description: Impeachment articles charge Congress never authorised the war on Iran, the $47bn bill is landing in the cost of living, and Europe should hold back defence money until Congress is back in charge of it.

item.title: Bomb hoaxes disrupt at least 18 flights across nine countries
item.description: Aer Lingus, Ryanair and Finnair flights were hit on 6 November. Searches found no explosives and all aircraft landed safely.

item.title: Dutch drone defence now runs on one US firm's software, bought without a race
item.description: Parliament stayed out, rivals stayed out, and a Dutch or European software answer exists so far only as the ministry's stated option. Experts warned of lost autonomy.

item.title: Russian strike on Komyshuvakha aid site, 43 dead and 53 missing
item.description: Zelensky says 43 bodies were recovered and 53 people are missing. Rescuers and police died in a second hit on a nearby shelter. The UN has condemned the strikes.

item.title: EU sets out first written accession roadmaps for four candidate countries
item.description: The Commission set out paths for Montenegro, Albania, Moldova and Ukraine and says candidates get access to selected areas of the single market before they join. Serbia made no substantive progress.

item.title: Russia says Europe cannot join Abu Dhabi talks on November 10-11
item.description: US envoy Steve Witkoff announced the talks. Kyiv wants an energy truce and a reopened Black Sea, and says it needs an extra 70 billion euros from Europe next year.

item.title: Schaeffler to cut 3,460 jobs in Europe and close five sites
item.description: About 2,660 posts go in Germany. The Herstal site closes with roughly 15 jobs lost.

item.title: Every appeal Meta files, Europe's small firms pay for twice
item.description: Two years of findings against Meta and TikTok, and still no final decision. Brussels must close the cases before national bans and patchwork rules do the job for it.

item.title: Russia lost ground in October; Kyiv counts record 54,400 casualties
item.description: Russian forces gave up a net 27.29 square kilometres for the second month running, even in Donetsk where the push is strongest.

item.title: North Korean hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, US agencies say
item.description: Crypto firms have frozen about $2.7 billion of the stolen funds. Binance says user funds are safe and it will cover all losses.

item.title: New York Times sues Brave over paywall bypass and AI content sales
item.description: The paper says Brave sold its journalism through its Search API and shipped a default paywall blocker. Other newspapers have filed their own suits in the same court.

item.title: Reporters Without Borders names Trump a press freedom predator
item.description: The group put him in its 2026 gallery of 33. The United States fell seven places to 64th of 180 countries.

item.title: French minister Darmanin warns Le Pen or Mélenchon win would end the EU
item.description: He told an audience in Barcelona a win for either would leave no European Community. The RN wants to cut France's 30.9 billion euro EU contribution the most, Le Figaro reports. France votes for president on 18 April.

item.title: EU split over strict checks on foreign IT suppliers ahead of Parliament debate
item.description: Member states want to keep the decisions for themselves. MEPs debate cyber resilience and critical infrastructure on Wednesday at 15:00.

item.title: Commission proposes €4.2 billion for Hungary and full Erasmus access
item.description: The Council has one month to decide on lifting the 2022 measures, which would also restore Hungarian access to Horizon Europe.

item.title: Poland caught up fast in the EU. The bill now sits on Warsaw's books.
item.description: Two decades of membership closed much of the gap with the EU, but the euros did less of that work than the price tag suggests. The deficits and debt are Poland's own, and the next round of costs is still up for grabs.

item.title: Hackers hit supermarket fridges across Europe again
item.description: The second attack in three weeks hit stores in France, Belgium, Sweden and the Netherlands. Intermarché's chief says France alone faces losses of tens of millions of euros in a day.

item.title: US troops and NATO cash on the line as Trump warns allies
item.description: The Pentagon has cancelled a brigade rotation to Poland and plans fewer troops in Germany, and diplomats fear more after the midterms. The White House points to the 5 percent spending deal.

item.title: Belgian government nears collapse over 10 billion euro budget hole
item.description: King Philippe is considering Prime Minister De Wever's resignation. If he accepts it, elections must follow within forty days.

item.title: EU and Canada agree deal short of membership
item.description: Diplomats say the deal drops the 'associate member' label Canada wanted, after Germany objected. It promises fewer trade barriers and a study on more Canadian LNG exports to Europe.

item.title: Hackers send false missile alerts through Ukraine's air warning app
item.description: The Air Alert app reached about 6.7 million users before developers shut it down and restored it within two hours. A Russian emergency ministry app was hit the next night.

item.title: Court orders Russian hockey teams back. Finland and Latvia refuse to play
item.description: The ruling covers all tournaments, including the 2027 World Championship in Germany. Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen says she will move to block Russian athletes from entering Finland.
